text.p: Bonds eased in line with other periphery markets but the shorter end remains well supported by expectations of a cut in the Bank of Portugal's repo rate of around 25 basis points on Friday, traders said.
Traders said that a cut in the repo rate would lead to a steepening of the yield curve.
"The short-end has more room to gain because it is looking for a lift from the Bank tomorrow and due to the 'super-escudo'," said one trader, refering to the rate expectations.

The Portuguese currency was firm against the mark although off its earlier highs when it had seemed set to break below 100 to the German currency. It closed at 100.11/14 against the opening 100.23/33.
